pictures.caption: Fig. 1. Jitter frequency of key points in different parts of real and fake faces. There are four broken lines in the figure, with the facial feature points of shaking taken from the eyes, nose, mouth, and outline. The green broken line represents the jitter frequency of the real FFPs, and the red broken line represents the jitter frequency of the fake FFPs.

pictures.path: parsed\deepfake detection using facial feature points\images\figure_002.png
pictures.caption: Fig. 2. General diagram of the FFP-ChT model. The input video frames are processed as a group and passed through BlazeFace for face detection and then through FaceMesh for the extraction of 468 FFPs. The extracted feature points are further calibrated by the FFP Re-Calibration algorithm, which computes a sequence of feature point displacements between frames. The FFP and FFP displacement sequences are separately fed into the ChT for training and the resulting predictions are combined for the final output. Conv, Convolutional layer; Conv2d, Two-Dimensional (2D) Convolutional layer; PReLU, Parametric Rectified Linear Unit.
